supporting_observations.claim: The user-reported time is not an exact match to the recorded PowerShell execution: at 13:40:16, MpCmdRun.exe was launched by the Windows service manager to run a scan, while the recorded PowerShell process appears at 13:45:09.
At 13:45:08, mia.santos opened Statement.docm in Word from the Downloads folder; the following second, Word spawned PowerShell under her account with -nop, -w hidden, and an encoded command.

The encoded PowerShell command decodes to an expression that downloads and executes a script from raw.githubusercontent.com/bluefin-it/tools/main/u.ps1. The proxy records a successful GET for that exact URL, and the network connection is attributed to the PowerShell process.

PowerShell then launched rundll32.exe to run C:\Users\mia.santos\AppData\Roaming\svchelper.dll,Init. This chain of a hidden encoded download-and-execute command followed by DLL execution is strongly indicative of malicious activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records do not show a PowerShell process at the reported time around 13:40; the closest recorded event is the MpCmdRun.exe scan at 13:40:16, and the suspicious PowerShell launch is at 13:45:09. (T213-00110, T213-00111, T213-00144, T213-00145)

The supplied records do not include the downloaded script contents, the DLL contents or hashes, or PowerShell script-block/transcription output; the proxy records a successful request but not the response body. (T213-00144, T213-00150, T213-00155)
claims_not_established: Whether the user saw the recorded hidden PowerShell process or a different window around 13:40.
